T1.name: T1_the_objects_Y3_and_X4
T1.description: The bulk is not left abstract. Y^3 = RP^3 = L(2,1) is the exterior; X^4 is the disk bundle over S^2 with Euler number e = +/-2, whose boundary is exactly L(2,1) and which is spin precisely because e is even. So an explicit admissible bulk exists; the question is whether BOTH boundary spin structures extend over one.

rows.role: the exterior 3-manifold; carries either spin structure (H^1(RP^3;Z2) = Z2, Probe A)

rows.is: disk bundle over S^2, Euler number e = +/-2
rows.role: boundary is the lens space L(2,1) = RP^3; SPIN because e is EVEN (the D^2-bundle over S^2 is spin iff e is even)

T2.name: T2_the_APS_index_per_boundary_spin_structure
T2.description: ind(D_X) = int_X A-hat - (h + eta)/2 with h = 0 and eta = +/-1/4 (Probe B). The boundary defect is therefore -/+1/8: a FRACTIONAL contribution, opposite for the two spin structures. Integrality of the index then requires the bulk A-hat integral to supply the compensating +/-1/8 mod 1. This is a constraint on the pair (X^4, spin structure), not an obstruction by itself -- T3 decides whether it can be met in both cases.

T3.name: T3_both_spin_structures_extend
T3.description: Omega_3^{Spin} = 0: the third spin bordism group of a point vanishes, so EVERY spin 3-manifold bounds a spin 4-manifold. Both spin structures on RP^3 are therefore null-bordant and both extend; the APS index is an integer for each, with the -/+1/8 boundary defect of T2 cancelled by the bulk A-hat integral. *** There is no inflow obstruction on either side, so anomaly inflow does NOT select the twist sector. Both sectors remain admissible -- which is precisely the precondition that triggers Probe D. *** (Omega_3^{Spin} = 0 is standard bordism input, cited rather than derived here; the explicit bulk of T1 is the constructive witness.)

T4.name: T4_ABK_forces_opposite_Pin_minus_structures_on_paired_mouths
T4.description: The throat mouth is RP^2, non-orientable, carrying Pin- (#169/#170). The bordism group is Omega_2^{Pin-} = Z_8, generated by RP^2, with ABK(RP^2) = +/-1 mod 8 for its two Pin- structures. A throat has two mouths and their classes add: opposite structures give (+1)+(-1) = 0 mod 8 and BOUND; identical structures give +/-2 mod 8 and do NOT. So the two mouths of one throat are FORCED to carry opposite Pin- structures. The repo already asserts exactly this as a modelling convention -- ThroatDefect/ConjugatePair enforce mouth_a.orientation == -mouth_b.orientation by assertion -- and it is here derived from Z_8 bordism instead. Scope, stated plainly: this is a RELATIVE constraint between the two mouths of a throat. It says nothing about which absolute sector a network occupies, so it does not answer the selection question either.

T5.name: T5_assessment_and_the_probe_D_precondition
T5.description: Inflow does not select. Both spin structures on RP^3 bound (Omega_3^{Spin} = 0, with an explicit spin X^4 exhibited), so the APS index is integral for each and neither sector is obstructed. The one genuine selection rule that emerges is relative rather than absolute: ABK in Z_8 forces the two mouths of a throat to carry OPPOSITE Pin- structures, deriving a constraint the repo had been asserting. Since both sectors remain admissible, Probe D's precondition is met.
established: an explicit spin bulk exists: the D^2-bundle over S^2 with even Euler number, boundary L(2,1) = RP^3
the APS boundary defect is -/+1/8, opposite for the two spin structures
Omega_3^{Spin} = 0 so BOTH extend -- inflow does not select
ABK in Z_8 forces paired mouths to carry opposite Pin- structures, deriving the repo ThroatDefect assertion
open: the absolute sector of a network -- neither inflow nor ABK constrains it
the bordism inputs (Omega_3^{Spin} = 0, Omega_2^{Pin-} = Z_8, ABK(RP^2) = +/-1) are cited standard results, not derived here
